//schema: A Warren FLOOR is PURE DATA. Fields: id,name,w,h,grid[strings of '#'wall/'.'floor],start[x,y],exit[x,y],hazards[[x,y]...] (tiles lethal ONLY while a patrol stands on them),patrol{path[[x,y]...],start:phaseIndex,mode:'pingpong'|'loop'},meta{accent,caption}. INVARIANT: the engine's stateKey MUST include the patrol phase (mod its period). IF a future floor adds a step-budget/timer or a stateful tile (a gate/latch), the stateKey MUST grow to include THAT too, or BFS dedupes two genuinely-different worlds as one. The monster is a pure function of phase and never reacts to you. NO-SOFTLOCK CONVENTION: the patrol PATH may extend over tiles the player can never stand on (cols 1..3 here are WALL to the player) — the monster walks 'off-stage' behind the wall, giving its excursion a longer beat. Only tiles that are BOTH floor AND in `hazards` can catch the player; keep every player-reachable floor tile on (or safely off) the forced path so no reachable live state is stranded — the solver's reverse-reachability check rejects a floor that softlocks.
name: THE CROSSING

meta.caption: The patrol is a fixed rhythm, not a hunter — it walks a longer beat than you can see, vanishing off-stage to the left behind the wall. Hold at the mouth of the corridor and cross on the beat its back is turned.
